data.title: Suspicious "vehicle data update fee" letter (Vorgang ZFD-26-118407)
data.summary: A letter from "Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland" claims that the vehicle data for plate MQ-BQ 207 has not been updated in over three years and demands an €89.00 "update fee" (Aktualisierungsgebühr) by 30 November 2026, threatening that the registration could be suspended from January 2027 and that non-payment will be reported to the registration office. This document shows strong signs of being a scam rather than an official German authority.
data.explanation: This letter is very likely a scam. There is no official German register called "Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland" — vehicle registrations are managed by your local Zulassungsstelle, which does not charge an "update fee" to a foreign bank account. The demanded payment goes to a Lithuanian (LT) IBAN under a private person's name, which is highly unusual for a German authority. Do not pay this fee. Before doing anything, verify independently by contacting your local Zulassungsstelle directly (not using the contact details on this letter) and consider reporting the letter to the police (Polizei) or consumer protection (Verbraucherzentrale). Keep the letter as evidence but do not transfer any money.

items.quote: Erfolgt keine Zahlung, melden wir den Vorgang der zuständigen Zulassungsstelle.

warnings: This letter claims to be from a "Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland", but no such official German vehicle register exists; vehicle registrations in Germany are handled by the local Zulassungsstelle, not a private postal address in Berlin.
The payment is requested to a Lithuanian (LT) IBAN made out to a private-sounding name, which is highly unusual and suspicious for a supposed German authority fee.

The urgent payment deadline combined with a threat that the registration will lapse is a typical pressure tactic used in scam letters; do not pay before independently verifying with your local Zulassungsstelle.
